rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so I raise SecurityGain and DiversityGain across the board to push obfuscation coverage while trimming cost sensitivity modestly rather than dramatically. This benchmark is C++ heavy on inlined templates, introsort and hand-tuned loop kernels (loop_unroll.cpp, stepanov_*.cpp), so RuntimeCost stays above SizeCost for FLA and BCF to keep the flattening/bogus-control-flow pressure off the hottest loop bodies while still allowing application to cold validation and reporting functions; IBR gets the highest SecurityGain since opaque-predicate branch insertion gives strong static-analysis resistance at moderate cost, and ICALL stays high because indirect dispatch blunts the call-graph recovery that matters for template-heavy Adobe-C++ code. SPLIT and IGV are weighted toward DiversityGain as cheap structure-level variance generators. CorrectnessRisk weights are held in the 0.25-0.4 band: not high enough to disable passes (round 0 showed the pipeline is stable on this sample) but sufficient to keep the riskiest rewrites, notably FLA and ICALL, off functions whose features signal fragile constructs like exception edges or va_args.
